text: ServiceNow compensation varies enormously by region, company size, industry, and whether a role is consulting or in-house. Any specific figure stated in this lesson would mislead a meaningful share of the people hearing it, and go stale within a year regardless. So instead of a number, this lesson teaches the method for finding your own honest one.

Walk into any compensation conversation already knowing a defensible range built from sources you can point to: public salary-survey sites, postings for comparable roles that list a real range, and professional communities where people in similar roles discuss actual figures. Triangulating across several sources gets you closer to reality than trusting any single site, since self-reported salary data is noisy.

Decide your walk-away point privately, before the conversation, not during it. Deciding in the moment, under stress or excitement about an offer, is how people either accept something they'll resent or ask for something unrealistic out of panic. A walk-away point set in advance, grounded in your researched range and your own real financial situation, keeps the conversation calm no matter which way it goes.

Base salary is the number most people fixate on, but it's one piece of a larger package: signing or relocation bonus, annual bonus structure and its real historical payout rather than just the target percentage, healthcare and retirement contributions, paid time off, remote-work flexibility, and start date. A company with limited room on base often has real room elsewhere, and asking about the full offer clearly and professionally — backed by the market research you already did — is simply good practice, not an aggressive tactic.

Whatever happens with one offer, keep your portfolio current and treat every interview as practice for the tradeoff-defense skill from Lesson 24 — it compounds with real project experience the same way Lesson 7 described on the path toward Technical Architect.
